question: Will the first dedicated bilateral US-China AI safety/security talks of Trump's second term be publicly confirmed to have taken place before September 18, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Reuters (Sept 4-5) reports a mid-September US-China AI safety dialogue is being prepared with Bessent leading, but the reporting is anonymous-sourced and explicitly not locked in. Two on-record US signals point away from the window: a White House official said there is 'currently no planned AI-related meeting in mid-September,' and Treasury said the sides 'may meet in October.' China published preconditions on Aug 31 demanding a shared definition of 'AI safety' first, a standoff that typically delays rather than accelerates. As of 2026-09-07, ~10 days before the deadline, no US or Chinese government readout or announcement exists (Treasury press releases show nothing on China/AI). The Sept 24 Trump-Xi Washington summit pulls any AI session toward the summit margins, i.e., after Sept 18. The resolution bar is additionally strict: a distinct AI-only bilateral session confirmed as having occurred, excluding summit agenda items and Track 1.5. Market check: no matching contract on Polymarket, Kalshi, or Manifold ('none found'); only a tangential Polymarket market on US blocking a Chinese AI model (~23%), which does not match this contract and is not used as an anchor. Small upside remains from a preparatory working-level AI-focused session being publicly confirmed ahead of the summit.
calls.reference_class: High-level bilateral diplomatic dialogues reported by wire services as tentatively planned for a specific ~2-week window, where an official of one government publicly states no such meeting is scheduled and no announcement exists ~10 days out
